Teaching is one of the most rewarding parts of my job. There's something deeply satisfying about watching a student go from "I don't understand R" to confidently analysing their own data, or seeing a field course spark someone's passion for ecology.

I believe in learning by doing, whether that means getting your hands dirty in the field or wrestling with real datasets in R. Theory matters, but it sticks better when you've experienced the messiness of actual ecological data.

![Field course at the Strait of Gibraltar](images/teaching-group.jpg){width=100% fig-alt="Field course with students"}

## Courses at UCM

### Undergraduate (BSc Biology)

- **Zoología**
- **Análisis de la Biodiversidad Animal**

### MSc in Conservation Biology

- **Caracterización y seguimiento de poblaciones animales amenazadas**: population monitoring and abundance estimation, including a hands-on module on distance sampling in R.
- **Evaluación Ambiental Aplicada a la Fauna**

### MSc in Zoology

- **Zoología de Vertebrados**

### Doctoral School

- **Introducción a la programación en R**: short course for PhD students of the UCM Doctoral School, taught with Daniel Ayllón. R fundamentals, data wrangling, reproducible reports with Quarto.

### Continuing education

- **[Aplicaciones Bioinformáticas en Biodiversidad, Ecología y Evolución](https://www.ucm.es/bioinformatica-biodiversidad)**: I coordinate this expert-level course (150 h, UCM título propio) that introduces biologists to computational tools for ecological and evolutionary analysis.

## Open materials

- [Quantitative Conservation Biogeography](https://damariszurell.github.io/EEC-QCB/): MSc course co-developed with [Damaris Zurell](https://damariszurell.github.io/) at the University of Potsdam. Species distribution models, connectivity and conservation planning in R.
- Tutorials on distance sampling and camera-trap occupancy models used in our MSc courses are available on request, and will be published here as they are cleaned up.

## Supervision

I supervise MSc and BSc theses every year, usually linked to our projects and datasets, and co-supervise with colleagues at UCM, UAM, UAH, UCLM and abroad. Current students and alumni are listed on the [People](people.html) page, together with information on how to [work with us](people.html#work-with-us).
